x.ASV: Michtam of David. Preserve me, O God; for in thee do I take refuge.
x.Darby: Michtam of David. Preserve me, OGod: for I trust in thee.
x.KJV: Michtam of David. Preserve me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust.
x.YLT: A Secret Treasure of David. Preserve me, O God, for I did trust in Thee.

nt: The superscription to this psalm identifies it as a **miktam**. Since the meaning of this word is not certain, you may wish to represent it in its Hebrew form and spell it the way it sounds in your language. See the discussion of that term in the Introduction to Psalms.
See how you translated the phrase “I take refuge” in [11:1](../011/001.md). Alternate translation: [I am safe because I trust in you] or [I depend on you to protect me]

x.ASV: O my soul, thou hast said unto Jehovah, Thou art my Lord: I have no good beyond thee.
x.Darby: Thou [my soul] hast said to Jehovah, Thou art the Lord: my goodness [extendeth] not to thee; —
x.KJV: O my soul, thou hast said unto the Lord, Thou art my Lord: my goodness extendeth not to thee;
x.YLT: Thou hast said to Jehovah, `My Lord Thou art;' My good is not for thine own sake;

nt: The pronoun **You** refers to David himself. If this is not clear for your readers, you could use David’s name here. Alternate translation: [David said to Yahweh]

By **my good is not beyond you**, David means that he does not experience happiness apart from Yahweh and does not experience material blessings or provision apart from Yahweh. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I have no good apart from you]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **good**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [both my happiness and material provision come from you]

x.ASV: As for the saints that are in the earth, They are the excellent in whom is all my delight.
x.Darby: To the saints that are on the earth, and to the excellent [thou hast said], In them is all my delight.
x.KJV: But to the saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent, in whom is all my delight.
x.YLT: For the holy ones who are in the land, And the honourable, all my delight is in them.

nt: The term **holy ones** refers to godly people or faithful believers. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [As for the godly people] or [As for the people who are faithful to Yahweh]

David is using the adjectives **holy** and **majestic** as nouns to mean certain kinds of people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [As for the holy people … the majestic people]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **delight**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [I fully delight in them]

x.ASV: Their sorrows shall be multiplied that give gifts for another god: Their drink-offerings of blood will I not offer, Nor take their names upon my lips.
x.Darby: Their sorrows shall be multiplied that hasten after another: their drink-offerings of blood will I not offer, and I will not take up their names into my lips.
x.KJV: Their sorrows shall be multiplied that hasten after another god: their drink offerings of blood will I not offer, nor take up their names into my lips.
x.YLT: Multiplied are their griefs, Who have hastened backward; I pour not out their libations of blood, Nor do I take up their names on my lips.

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **sorrows**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [They will suffer greatly, they who hasten after another god]

The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You could supply these words from the context, as in the ULT, if it would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [those who hasten after another god]

Here David is speaking as if those who seek out and eagerly worship other gods actually **hasten after** them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they who worship another god]

By **I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood**, the psalmist means that he will not participate in the pagan worship practices that involve offering drinks mixed with blood to false gods. You could include this information in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I will not participate in their blood offerings to other gods]

Here, **lips** represents speaking or saying something aloud. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will not speak their names] or [and I will not say their names]

x.ASV: Jehovah is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: Thou maintainest my lot.
x.Darby: Jehovah is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou maintainest my lot.
x.KJV: The Lord is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou maintainest my lot.
x.YLT: Jehovah is the portion of my share, and of my cup, Thou--Thou dost uphold my lot.

nt: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the phrase **my cup** before the phrases **the portion of my inheritance** and **holding my lot**. Alternate translation: [my cup. You are the portion of my inheritance, and you are holding my lot] or [you are my cup. You are the portion of my inheritance, and you are holding my lot]

By saying that Yahweh is **my cup** David could mean: (1) that Yahweh controls his destiny in which case he uses **cup** to refer to what one drinks and therefore, metaphorically, to what one receives in life. Alternate translation: [and the one who controls my future], or (2) [provision] in which case **cup** refers to physical provision. Alternate translation: [and the one who gives me great blessings]

Here David is speaking of Yahweh as if he were actually **the portion of my inheritance**. David is alluding to the inheritance of and distribution of land. (See the Introduction to this psalm for more information.) He means that Yahweh is his most valuable possession and the source of all his blessings and sustenance. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my most precious possession, my source of blessing]

Here David is speaking as if God were literally **holding** his lot, as if his destiny were a physical object that could be grasped in someone’s hand. He means that God controls and secures his future. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You are maintaining my lot] or [You are maintaining my destiny]

x.ASV: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; Yea, I have a goodly heritage.
x.Darby: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage.
x.KJV: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage.
x.YLT: Lines have fallen to me in pleasant places, Yea, a beauteous inheritance is for me.

nt: חֲבָלִ֣ים נָֽפְלוּ־לִ֭⁠י בַּ⁠נְּעִמִ֑ים אַף־נַ֝חֲלָ֗ת שָֽׁפְרָ֥ה עָלָֽ⁠י

Here David is speaking as if his inheritance from God were actually **measuring cords** (used to divide land) that **have fallen** (were put) in **pleasant places**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. If not, you could state this as a comparison or in plain language. Alternate translation: [God has given me a delightful inheritance; indeed, what I have received is wonderful]

x.ASV: I will bless Jehovah, who hath given me counsel; Yea, my heart instructeth me in the night seasons.
x.Darby: I will bless Jehovah, who giveth me counsel; even in the nights my reins instruct me.
x.KJV: I will bless the Lord, who hath given me counsel: my reins also instruct me in the night seasons.
x.YLT: I bless Jehovah who hath counselled me; Also in the nights my reins instruct me.

nt: Here the word the ULT translates as **even** could: (1) be adding an additional thought. Alternate translation: [also,] or (2) be functioning to emphasize or assert what follows it. Alternate translation: [indeed]

Here the **kidneys** represent where a person’s thoughts and conscience exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language that you could use, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my mind instructs me]

David is speaking of **my kidneys** as if they were a living thing that could **instruct** him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh instructs my mind]

Here David assumes that readers will know that when he speaks of his mind instructing him, this happens as he thinks about Yahweh and what is pleasing to Yahweh, and probably also as he prays. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [my mind instructs me as I think about Yahweh] or [my mind instructs me as I pray and think about Yahweh]

x.ASV: I have set Jehovah always before me: Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
x.Darby: I have set Jehovah continually before me; because [he is] at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
x.KJV: I have set the Lord always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
x.YLT: I did place Jehovah before me continually, Because--at my right hand I am not moved.

nt: The implication is that David is deliberately making Yahweh his constant focus and priority in life. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I constantly focus on Yahweh] or [In all that I do I am conscious of Yahweh]

David is using **he is at my right hand** as a common expression of his culture to mean “he is helping me” or “he is protecting me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he is helping me] or [he is protecting me]
See how you translated the similar expression in [15:5](../015/005.md).

This is a double negative. David uses the negative particle **not**, with the negative word **shaken** to express a positive meaning strongly. The phrase **I will not be shaken** means that David will remain firm and secure. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [he makes me live securely]

x.ASV: Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: My flesh also shall dwell in safety.
x.Darby: Therefore my heart rejoiceth, and my glory exulteth; my flesh moreover shall dwell in hope.
x.KJV: Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope.
x.YLT: Therefore hath my heart been glad, And my honour doth rejoice, Also my flesh dwelleth confidently:

nt: These two phrases **my heart is glad** and **my glory rejoices** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [my heart is glad, yes, my whole being rejoices] or [my heart is glad, yes, my glory rejoices]

Here the **heart** represents where a person’s emotions exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am glad] or [I feel glad]

Here, **glory** represents David’s “spirit” and by extension his feelings that come from his spirit (inner person). If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I rejoice]

Here, **flesh** represents David himself, specifically his body. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will dwell]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **security**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [securely]

x.ASV: For thou wilt not leave my soul to Sheol; Neither wilt thou suffer thy holy one to see corruption.
x.Darby: For thou wilt not leave my soul to Sheol, neither wilt thou allow thy Holy One to see corruption.
x.KJV: For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.
x.YLT: For Thou dost not leave my soul to Sheol, Nor givest thy saintly one to see corruption.

nt: David is using one part of himself, his **soul**, to mean all of him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me]
לֹא־תַעֲזֹ֣ב נַפְשִׁ֣⁠י לִ⁠שְׁא֑וֹל לֹֽא־תִתֵּ֥ן חֲ֝סִידְ⁠ךָ֗ לִ⁠רְא֥וֹת שָֽׁחַת

These two phrases **you will not abandon my soul to Sheol** and **You will not hand over your godly one to see the pit** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [you will save me, your faithful follower, from death] or [you will save me, a godly person, from the grave]
לֹא־תַעֲזֹ֣ב נַפְשִׁ֣⁠י לִ⁠שְׁא֑וֹל לֹֽא־תִתֵּ֥ן חֲ֝סִידְ⁠ךָ֗ לִ⁠רְא֥וֹת שָֽׁחַת

See the Introduction to this psalm for a discussion of this phrase. Here, David is referring to Yahweh saving him from evil men who might try to kill him. David is not saying that he will not die of old age. Avoid translating this verse in a way that might make it appear that David thinks he will not die of old age.

David assumes that readers will know that **the pit** refers to the grave or death. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [You will rescue your godly one from death] or [You will rescue your godly one from the grave]

Even though David is addressing Yahweh directly, he is speaking of himself in the third person as **your godly one** to show humility. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a humble form in the first person. Alternate translation: [me, your godly one]

t: you will make known to/ me

x.ASV: Thou wilt show me the path of life: In thy presence is fulness of joy; In thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
x.Darby: Thou wilt make known to me the path of life: thy countenance is fulness of joy; at thy right hand are pleasures for evermore.
x.KJV: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
x.YLT: Thou causest me to know the path of life; Fulness of joys is with Thy presence, Pleasant things by Thy right hand for ever!

nt: Here David is speaking of how to live as if it were actually **the path**. The phrase **of life** indicates he is speaking of living in a way that results in a joyful and blessed life in the present and in the future. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [how to live in a way that results in me being joyful and blessed, both now and in the future]

Here, **before your face** represents being in Yahweh’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [are in your presence … are joys] or [are with you … are pleasures]

Here, **right hand** represents God’s power and ability to give something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [are before … with you are delights forever] or [are before … you give delights forever]
